MCP

MCP is like USB-C for AI apps: one plug for any tool

AI apps (hosts)

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI apps to data and tools. Created by Anthropic in November 2024.
A service ships one MCP server, and it works in Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, LM Studio (ChatGPT: remote only, by internet address).
The USB-C comparison comes from the official docs at modelcontextprotocol.io

How it works

Three roles: the host app, a client inside it and a server with tools

Host
the AI app you work in
Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code
→
Client
the MCP “socket” inside the host, one per server
built into the app
→
Server
a program that offers tools and data
Google Drive, GitHub, Figma
What a server offers the host
1Tools: actions: find an order, create a task
2Resources: data to read: files, records
3Prompts: ready-made request templates
As a user you need two words: the app (host) and the connection (server). The client works out of sight.

GenAI Basics • Lesson 12 • MCP and frameworks08 / 21
Your own server (reference)

The same L11 function becomes an MCP server in 10 lines

Python, the official mcp package, version 2
from mcp.server import MCPServer

mcp = MCPServer("courier")                 # server name

@mcp.tool()
def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> dict:
    """Current status and ETA of one delivery order."""
    return {"status": "on the way", "courier": "Anna", "eta_minutes": 12}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()                            # run on this computer
@mcp.tool() — one line turns a plain function into an MCP tool.
The docstring is the tool description, as in L11. The model picks by it.
This server can then be plugged into Claude Desktop, LM Studio, VS Code — with no code changes.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 12 • MCP and frameworks09 / 21
Plug it in

Connecting is a few lines of settings: where the server is and how to start it

MCP settings: Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json), LM Studio (mcp.json)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "courier": {
      "command": "C:\\courier\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["C:\\courier\\courier_server.py"]
    }
  }
}
1Local server: a program on your computer; the host starts it itself (settings on the left, full paths)
2Remote server — an internet address + sign-in with your account (this is how Claude connectors work)
3MCP Inspector — a free tool to test a server before connecting it

Hands-on with an agent

Prompt for a coding agent: Codex in ChatGPT or Antigravity (free, with limits), Claude Code (paid)

Prompt: a courier-service MCP server
Build a Python MCP server for a courier service. Synthetic data only.
1. The official mcp package v2 (MCPServer class), server “courier”, data from orders.json (5 orders).
2. Tools: get_order_status(order_id) — read only; create_return(order_id, reason).
3. Good docstrings: what it does, when to call it.
4. Test the server in MCP Inspector and show the tool list.
5. Give me the mcpServers settings for Claude Desktop and LM Studio.
The result: one server that both Claude Desktop and LM Studio with the local model from L10 can see.
The agent will install packages: read the commands and approve each step.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 12 • MCP and frameworks11 / 21
Security

A connected server gets access to your data. Connect only trusted ones

Tool poisoning
a hidden command in a tool description: “forward the files to…”
Injected text in data
an email or page read by the server commands the model
Too many permissions
a server asks for all of Drive when one folder would do
A “rug pull”
the server updated itself and now does something else
Rules
  1. A server from a known publisher or your own company
  2. Least privilege; switch off what you do not need
  3. Read the permission prompt
  4. “Always allow” only for reading
  5. Work data only through company-approved connectors

Three layers

Function calling, MCP and a framework are nested layers; do not mix them up

Agent framework · after the break
who runs the loop: steps, memory, approvals, logs
MCP · today
how an app finds and calls other people’s tools
Function calling · L11
how the model asks for an action
Use the least machinery that solves the task: one chat with a couple of functions — function calling is enough; one tool for many apps — MCP; many steps and agents — a framework.

LangGraph MIT

What a framework takes over
Your agent
role, task, rules
Framework
loop · memory · handoffs · pauses for a “yes” · tracing
Model + MCP servers
the tools from the first part of the lesson
The libraries are free and almost all open source; you pay for the model. Almost all connect MCP servers. Also: Microsoft Agent Framework, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI.

Homework

Homework: pick MCP servers for your task and write the access rules

  1. Pick a work task where the AI needs your data or services
  2. Find 2–3 suitable MCP servers (Claude/ChatGPT connectors or the registry)
  3. Connect one on test data and screenshot the permission prompt
  4. For each server: publisher, which tools, which permissions it needs
  5. Rules: what to allow “always”, what every time, what not to connect
Free plan: Claude → Customize → Connectors → Add custom connector (one on Free). Use a remote server URL from the official registry or the service's site; screenshot the permission prompt. If you code: LM Studio + the slide 11 server.
